idea-plugin.name: Spring Config Drift Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Catch broken environment configuration before it reaches production. This plugin compares every application*.yml, application*.properties, .env, and docker-compose*.yml file across your profiles and reports what a code review alone tends to miss.

What it finds

  • Missing keys — set in some environments, silently absent from others, with default-profile inheritance handled correctly. Comparisons stay scoped within one config system (Spring / .env / Compose), so a Spring-only key is never reported missing from an .env-only profile. The Key Matrix marks those cells as ~ (not applicable)
  • Shape drift — the same key is a number in one environment and a string, list, or nested object in another — including a scalar in one profile versus a list of objects in another
  • Exposed secrets — passwords, tokens, API keys, private keys, and credentials embedded in URLs. Values are masked the moment they are detected and are never stored, logged, or written to a report. Correctly externalized values (${DB_PASSWORD}, or postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@…) are left alone; only what is actually committed (including non-blank placeholder defaults) is flagged
  • Unresolved placeholders — ${DB_HOST} references with no default and nothing in the project to supply them
  • Metadata contract violations — cross-checked against spring-configuration-metadata.json and, when present, your own @ConfigurationProperties classes (Java and Kotlin) for keys declared but never set, set but never declared, and simple type mismatches

Relaxed binding is understood, so driver-class-name, driverClassName, and DRIVER_CLASS_NAME count as one property rather than three. Profiles that only override a handful of keys are recognised as partial overlays within each config system instead of being reported as incomplete environments; that judgement can be overridden per profile in Settings | Tools | Config Drift.

Every finding jumps to the exact key in the exact file. Inline highlights and the tool window refresh automatically a couple of seconds after you save a config file — or after a config file or folder is moved, renamed, or deleted. Results export as Markdown for a pull request or JSON for a CI gate.

Scope

This is static comparison plus a lightweight metadata contract check — it does not reimplement the Spring Binder (nested properties inside a list/map of a custom type aren't modeled, only the container itself), resolve SpEL, Vault, or Config Server values, read your real environment variables, or modify your files. @ConfigurationProperties reading is a syntactic PSI walk, not semantic type resolution — for Kotlin classes specifically, this means a nested property is only followed into a type declared in the same file.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.1

  • New: headless config-drift CLI on GitHub Releases for CI gates (check --fail-on error|warning|never, exit codes 0/1/2)
  • New: optional repo file .config-drift.yml for shared CLI defaults (fail-on, path, profiles.complete / profiles.overlay); explicit CLI flags still win. IDE Settings remain separate
  • New: CLI --format sarif for GitHub Code Scanning, and --no-matrix for shorter Markdown suitable for sticky PR comments
  • New: sample GitHub Action that posts a sticky Markdown report on the PR and uploads SARIF (see docs/examples/github-action-config-drift.yml)
  • Analysis engine split into :core / :cli / IntelliJ plugin modules; IDE behaviour unchanged for drift findings, matrix, and suppressions

0.2.0

  • New: .env files are compared across profiles alongside application*.yml/.properties — including missing-key, shape-drift, and secret detection. Profiles follow the dotenv convention (.env, .env.production, .env.production.local)
  • New: docker-compose.yml / compose.yml support — each service's environment: block is checked, keyed per service (web.DB_HOST vs worker.DB_HOST). Profiles follow the filename; env_file: references are not followed. Compose ${VAR:-default} defaults are understood alongside Spring's ${VAR:default}
  • New: comparisons are scoped per config system (Spring / .env / Compose), so a Spring-only key is never reported missing from an .env-only profile; the Key Matrix uses ~ for not-applicable cells
  • New: metadata contract checks also read project @ConfigurationProperties classes (Java and Kotlin), not only spring-configuration-metadata.json. Kotlin uses a syntactic PSI walk — nested types are only followed when declared in the same file. Depends on the bundled Java and Kotlin plugins
  • Secret detection also recognises underscore-separated key names (DB_PASSWORD, API_KEY)
  • Fixed Key Matrix cells wrongly showing inherited (^) across config systems
  • Fixed scalar-vs-list-of-object shape conflicts when YAML flattens indexed children as app.items[0].name
  • Fixed secret false positives on correctly externalized JDBC URLs such as postgresql://${DB_USER}:${DB_PASSWORD}@…
  • Fixed automatic re-analysis when a folder containing config files is moved, renamed, or deleted
  • Fixed partial-overlay detection to judge peers per config system
  • Fixed Kotlin cross-file nested types producing spurious declared-but-never-set INFO findings when only nested children are set

0.1.1

  • Fixed a race where dismissing a finding while an automatic re-analysis was in flight could make the dismissed finding silently reappear
  • Fixed a performance issue where every VFS change event in the IDE (not just config file changes) triggered a virtual file resolution, needlessly on the EDT
  • Fixed a caching bug where a metadata file that failed to read once could stay incorrectly cached as empty until its next unrelated change
  • Fixed a potential crash in the Key Matrix tool window when the profile set changes
  • Config file discovery order is now deterministic across runs
  • The Copy Report toolbar buttons now show a brief confirmation when the report is copied to the clipboard
  • "Analyze Spring Config Drift" is now also available by right-clicking an application*.yml/.properties file, in the Project view or the editor
  • A partial-overlay finding's Location column now names the Settings page it jumps to, instead of showing "—" as if the row led nowhere

0.1.0

  • First release: cross-profile comparison of YAML and properties configuration
  • Missing key, shape drift, secret exposure, unresolved placeholder, and metadata contract detection
  • Findings and key-matrix tool window with jump-to-source
  • Markdown and JSON report export
  • Partial-overlay profile detection, overridable in Settings | Tools | Config Drift

action.description: Compare application*.yml/.properties, .env, and docker-compose files across profiles and report drift
